Halsin is a recruitable Companion who can be romanced by characters of any gender. He is a wood elf and a Circle of the Moon Druid with the Outlander background. Halsin can first be found in the Shattered Sanctum during Act One as an attached follower or as a camp follower.

Halsin seeks to create a harmonious balance between nature and civilisation as well as find a cure for the Shadow Curse that has haunted his home for the past century.

“
I'm 350 years old. Of course there have been lovers. Just because I love nature doesn't mean I'm betrothed to it...
„
— Halsin, on his sex life

Overview

Background

Halsin is the Archdruid of the Emerald Grove and an accomplished healer. Before he went missing, Halsin and his apprentice  Nettie were researching the recent cases of illithid tadpole infections.

Starting class

Before he is recruited, Halsin can first be met in the Worg Pens of the Shattered Sanctum as a level 5 druid, wildshaped into a bear with the following ability scores: 20 STR, 10 DEX, 16 CON, 10 INT, 17 WIS, 13 CHA. If he is freed and met later in the Emerald Grove, his ability scores are: 16 STR, 11 DEX, 14 CON, 10 INT, 17 WIS, 13 CHA. If he is recruited in Act Two, Halsin reverts to a level 1 druid with the standard ability scores for that class. His subclass is Circle of the Moon, specialised in wildshaping into various creatures to attack enemies or support allies in combat.

Personal quest

Halsin does not have a Companion Quest. He is, however, deeply tied to ⁠Lift the Shadow Curse, and it cannot be successfully completed without his assistance.

Recruitment

To recruit Halsin, the quests ⁠Defeat the Goblins, ⁠Rescue the Druid Halsin, and ⁠Save the First Druid must be completed with him alive, and he must agree to join the party as they travel to the Shadow-Cursed Lands. Halsin can be recruited in Act Two after the party progress in the quest to lift the Shadow Curse to a certain point. However, if they proceed to Act Three without fully completing the quest, Halsin stays behind in the Shadow-Cursed Lands. Recruiting Halsin grants the ⁠Patrician of the Grove inspiration to party members with the  Noble background.

Approval

Main article: Halsin/Approval

Halsin only gains or loses approval once he joins the party as a full companion. He likes those who are kind, especially to animals or children, and dislikes any decisions that involve harming the natural world or supporting corruption and cruelty.

Romance

Main article: Halsin/Romance

Halsin can be romanced. Though the majority of his romance occurs in Act Three, he can be flirted with in prior Acts. He is polyamorous and is the only companion who may be romanced in later stages alongside  Astarion,  Shadowheart, or  Karlach – with their consent.

Description

Appearance

As a wood elf, Halsin stands out among his people, having an unusually tall and heavy athletic build. His chest and shoulders are broad, and his body thick with muscle, yet he retains a relaxed but ready stance. He has a deep, even voice and typically keeps a calm demeanour as reflected by his undisturbed face. He has warm two-toned eyes, gray with a touch of brown, along with a square jaw, straight nose, high cheekbones, and long, pointed ears. He has large calloused hands and sun-browned skin, marked by a few pale scars along the arms and ribs. He has chestnut brown hair, worn long and usually tied back, with a few loose strands at the temples. His movements are unhurried and balanced, the stride of someone used to long days in the wild. Despite (and perhaps because of) these traits, his presence typically feels steady and protective rather than aggressive. With all of these qualities, Halsin is generally found quite attractive and handsome and, like many who are so desired, has had his share of trials as a result.

At camp, he favours simple leathers and a green cloak with a fur-lined collar, worn over a shoulder harness and bracers. Oak leaf clasps, a druidic torc, and a bear claw charm finish the look. When travelling, he switches to sturdier druid leathers in forest shades with leaf and root motifs, tall boots, and practical belts for pouches and tools, all of which add to his imposing outdoorsman presence.

Personality

Despite his tenacity in combat, Halsin is a gentle, honest elf who treasures the sanctity and beauty of nature. Despite being a powerful healer with a lofty title, Halsin is humble and patient – though he is willing to act with force if the need arises. One of Halsin's core beliefs is that desire should flourish wherever it finds purchase. He views carnal pleasures as a natural calling and monogamy, while something to be cherished, as something which suits others more so than himself.

History

Many years ago, when Halsin was younger and far more foolhardy than he is now, he ventured to the Underdark to experience the beauty of its unworldly flora. Instead, he found himself captured by a noble Drow house – in his words, "something between guest, prisoner, and consort". The house's matron and patron took an interest in him, seeing a bristling, well-formed wood elf from the surface as quite the novelty, and he spent nearly three years chained in their bedchamber.

Halsin did what was necessary to survive the experience, though he does not look negatively upon it, because while he feared for his life, he is proud he was able and willing to wait for the chance to regain his freedom. That chance came when his captors' rivals attacked, as  Lolth's noble houses are constantly at each other's throats. While the drow were distracted by the battle, he escaped, though he never learned what became of his 'hosts'.

One hundred years before the events of the game, Halsin was part of the Emerald Grove's forces in the attack against  Ketheric Thorm at Moonrise Towers. However, shortly after Ketheric's body was interred within the Grand Mausoleum, the shadow curse took hold. In the chaos that followed, Halsin lost contact with  Thaniel, his childhood friend and the living spirit of the land. Worse still, the Archdruid of the Emerald Grove was lost to the curse, leaving Halsin to take command and lead the survivors to safety.

Gameplay

For full information on Halsin's starting features, see Druid and Elf.

As a druid, Halsin is capable of filling a variety of roles in the party. He can debilitate enemies with control spells, support the party with spells that enhance himself and his allies, and deal damage with elemental damage-dealing spells. His  Wild Shape feature allows him to wade into battle as a melee combatant or sneak and scout as a small animal.

Skills with Proficiency

  •  Animal Handling
  •  Nature
  •  Perception
  •  Stealth
  •  Survival

Temporary companion features

As a temporary companion, he knows the following spells:

  •  Call Lightning
  •  Healing Word
  •  Misty Step
  •  Thunderwave
  •  Wild Shape: Cave Bear

Permanent companion features

Halsin always has  Wild Shape: Cave Bear, which can be used by a non-druid Halsin by equipping the  Shapeshifter Hat for the  Wild Shape Charge. If Halsin has no 2nd-level spell slots,  Lunar Mend can be cast at 1st level without expending a spell slot.

Halsin also always has the  Healing Word and  Thunderwave spells prepared, even if he is not a spellcaster. As long as he has no 2nd-level spell slots (including warlock spell slots and spell slots from an Elixir of Arcane Cultivation), these spells are free to cast. For example, if Halsin is a level 12 monk, a barbarian 10/druid 2, or an Arcane Trickster 6/Battle Master 4/warlock 2, he can cast these two spells for free. As soon as Halsin gets a 2nd-level spell slot, the spells consume spell slots normally.

At druid level 3, Halsin gets  Misty Step always prepared; this spell is free of cost as long as he has no 3rd-level spell slots. This means that Halsin as a druid 3/paladin 2 can use Misty Step for free, but he does not have it for free as a druid 3/wizard 2.

Finally, Halsin has  Call Lightning always prepared at druid level 5. Similarly, the spell has no cost as long as he does not have 4th-level spell slots.

When respeccing and levelling up Halsin, his innate spells may need to be added to his hotbar from his spellbook. When casting these spells with without spell slots, they are always cast at their base level. When cast with spell slots, they can be upcast as normal.

These four spells are considered 'granted' spells, so they use Halsin's current spellcasting ability at the time he receives them. Halsin loses access to these spells when he changes form, including using  Wild Shape and  Disguise Self, though not  Starry Form. When Halsin returns to his normal form, all these spells are re-granted, which causes all of Halsin's granted spells to change to the spellcasting ability of the most recently acquired class (See Item spellcasting ability for a detailed explanation).

Involvement

Act One

Halsin joined  Aradin's ill-fated expedition to find the  Nightsong, hoping to find a way to reach Moonrise Towers and the Shadow-Cursed Lands. However, he was captured and can be saved by the party; he is imprisoned in the Worg Pens within the Shattered Sanctum, and is being harassed by nearby goblins, who throw stones at him while he remains in wildshape.

When his cage is approached, a dialogue cutscene is triggered. The goblins Three, One and Brawler Birka harass the wildshaped Halsin, thinking he is just a bear, and plan to kill him to feed the worgs. If a party member has  Speak with Animals active, they can speak to the 'bear', who will ask for help. Various outcomes are possible:

  • The party can join the harassment and throw a stone at him, in which case he breaks free of the pen, instantly kills Birka, and attacks the goblins and the party. The goblins then are allied with the party in this fight.
  • The goblins can be urged to stop their harassment, but they refuse, and as in the previous case, Halsin breaks free and instantly kills Birka. In the fight that breaks out, Halsin is allied with the party against the goblins.
  • A party member can use the  Illithid Persuasion to order the goblins to stop and release the bear. The pen is unlocked, and Halsin immediately moves to kill the goblins. The party can chose to join him and attack the goblins, attack him and join the goblins, or leave him at the mercy of the goblins, which counts as allying with the goblins.

If the party ally with him, Halsin offers to help in seeking a cure for their tadpole problem, but first asks them to ⁠defeat the goblin leaders to protect the Grove. While he can join the party as a temporary companion at this point, he attacks the rest of the goblins on sight, so if discretion is preferred, he can be asked to wait in the Worg Pens. If the party kill the goblin leaders before they enter the Worg Pens for the first time, Halsin may break out by himself and return to the Emerald Grove.

If Halsin is killed, ⁠Rescue the Druid Halsin can be progressed by using  Speak with Dead on his corpse.

After the goblin leaders are defeated, Halsin returns to the Emerald Grove, where he confronts  Kagha based on the party's choices when they ⁠investigate her actions.

The morning following the tiefling's celebration, Halsin tells the party about the two leads he has on how to reach the Shadow-Cursed Lands: travelling through the Mountain Pass, which would be less dangerous at first but would mean a longer journey through the shadow curse, or exploring the Underdark in search of an alternative route, which would bypass some of the shadow curse but comes with all the dangers inherent there.

Regardless of which option the player character suggests exploring, Halsin accompanies the party as a Camp Follower in the hopes of travelling to the Shadow-Cursed Lands and lifting the Shadow Curse afflicting the region.

If the party proceed to the Rosymorn Monastery Trail or the Shadow-Cursed Lands before rescuing Halsin from the Goblin Camp, his dead body remains in his cell.

Act Two

Halsin provides vital assistance in the process of lifting the Shadow Curse, and it cannot be completed if he dies. He asks that the party keep an eye out for any information regarding a boy called  Thaniel, who is in fact the land's spirit.

Once Halsin is given a lead to Thaniel's location by  Art Cullagh (whether through waking him or using  Speak with Dead on his corpse), he performs a ritual to open a portal to the Shadowfell and leaves to retrieve the boy. If the party fail to protect the portal from the waves of shadow-cursed creatures, it closes, and Halsin is lost to the Shadowfell forever.

If Thaniel is successfully rescued from the Shadowfell and Thaniel's other half,  Oliver, is also convinced to reunite with him, Halsin offers to join the party for the remainder of Act Two. He becomes a permanent companion if  Ketheric Thorm is defeated and the Shadow Curse is lifted upon leaving the Shadow-Cursed Lands.

Act Three

Halsin has no direct involvement in any Act Three storyline, though taking him out of the Lower City campsite and speaking with him has him express fear that balancing nature and civilisation may not even be possible. He is also one of two companions (alongside  Astarion) who can have a foursome at Sharess' Caress without having been romanced, and he tells the player character about his experience with the noble drow after participating. Lastly, he is added to ⁠Gather Your Allies, harnessing Thaniel's strength to provide the  Spirit of the Land condition once the party reaches the Upper City.

Halsin is also one of  Orin's potential abduction targets. If  Lae'zel is dead, romanced, or in the active party upon first long resting in the Lower City, Orin instead captures Halsin and infiltrates the camp disguised as him, pretending to have gone mad and almost killed  Scratch. Depending on how this scenario is resolved, he either gets killed by Orin before the player character's battle with her or returns to the party afterwards.

Endings

Alone with the Shadow Curse

If the party fail or neglect to complete ⁠Lift the Shadow Curse, Halsin stays in the Shadow-Cursed Lands and continues studying the curse on his own. He sees the player character off at the Road to Baldur's Gate, but he is never seen again in Act Three. If the player character recruits Halsin by freeing Thaniel but does not reunite Thaniel with Oliver, Halsin still permanently leaves the party, taking whatever equipment he is currently wearing with him.

Life as a new father

Otherwise, if the party lift the Shadow Curse and Halsin is not killed by Orin, he returns to Reithwin Town after defeating the Netherbrain to help the former Shadow-Cursed Lands continue healing. He keeps in touch with Thaniel and Oliver, resumes his hobby of whittling, and converts Moonrise Towers into an orphanage, where he adopts and raises nine wagons of children who were orphaned by the Shadow Curse and the Absolute. When spoken to at the Epilogue reunion celebration, he asks the player character for bedtime story ideas and gifts them a  Whittled Duck; the player character can ask him to take the  Owlbear Cub in return as a pet for the children.

If the player character romanced Halsin, they can offer to move in with him and help with the children, and at the reunion party, he asks if they are comfortable having settled down after adventuring for so long. If the player character also partnered with Astarion or  Shadowheart, they maintain a long-distance relationship with whichever partner they did not stay with. If the player character also partnered with  Karlach, however, they cannot stay with Halsin unless she dies. If the player character instead went to Avernus with Karlach (as a friend or as a second partner), they can apologise to Halsin at the reunion party for leaving so abruptly, but he forgives them and says he will always be there when they get back. The player character can respond by embracing and kissing him or by amicably thanking him; either way, Halsin then shares about his new life as he would if not romanced.

Speak with Dead

Halsin's corpse can be communed with using  Speak with Dead. The dialogue varies depending on whether he was abducted and killed by Orin or not, as well as on how far the story has advanced when he is killed:

  • Who are you?
    • Halsin
      Halsin... First Druid...
  • What happened to you? (Act 1 only)
    • Halsin
      Captured... goblins... drow... killed...
  • What can you tell me about ceremorphosis?
    • Halsin
      Altered... arrested... unnatural magic...
      • Magic? What magic?
        • Halsin
          Someone controls the parasites... controls the cultists...
          • Who controls the parasites?
            • Halsin
              Unknown... powerful magic... Moonrise Towers...
              • Moonrise Towers? How do I get there?
                • Halsin
                  Follow Chionthar... but beware... danger ahead... darkness...
                  • Darkness? What do you mean?
                    • Halsin
                      Curse... made of shadow... all succumb to it... find another way...
                      • Halsin
                        Secret tunnel... entrance hidden... Selûne temple...
  • Where are your valuables?
    • Halsin
      Study... hidden... Emerald Grove...

If Halsin was abducted and killed by Orin:

  • Who are you?
    • Halsin
      Halsin... First Druid... surely you knew that by now...?
  • How did you end up here?
    • Halsin
      Orin... abducted me from camp... so strong...
  • How did you meet your end?
    • Halsin
      Orin's blades.
      • Halsin
        I hoped my loved would save me... (if romanced)
      • Halsin
        I hoped my friends would save me... (if not romanced)
  • What was your purpose?
    • Halsin
      Stop the Netherbrain. Help my friends... as they helped me.
  • Do you have any regrets?
    • Halsin
      Thaniel and Oliver... I never said goodbye. Never saw their land flourish...

Notes and references

  • Halsin was not originally slated to be a companion, but due to his popularity among fans, Larian Studios decided to add him as one.
  • Halsin did not obtain his large facial scar in battle, but rather was marked by a she-bear encountered while in wildshape during mating season, who attacked after being rejected. This can be brought up as his greatest failure during the Test Your Love game with  Zethino, though he will be disappointed and scold that "Rejecting unwanted advances is no failure, even if it earned me some scars."
  • Halsin is noted to be much larger than normal for a wood elf, and speculates he may have some orc in his family tree.
  • Halsin's surname is Silverbough according to his main writer John Corcoran: "While there’s nothing in the game itself, an earlier character outline stated it was Silverbough. This is probably semi-canon at best as there’s nothing supporting or contradicting it in the game." He goes on to note: "I do still like it as it alludes to an aspect of Celtic mythology that has nice thematic resonance for Halsin and Thaniel (the silver bough or branch granting access to the land of eternal youth)." (Twitter/X post from November 30, 2023 and the subsequent post)
  • There is a cut out camp scene in which Halsin demands  Minthara to be kicked out of the party, despite knowing this would result in her being enthralled by The Absolute, as she would no longer be protected by the Mysterious Artefact. The scene is scripted, animated, and voiced, but left out of the game. If the player character chose to let Minthara stay, Halsin would say he will remain until the Shadow Curse is dealt with.
  • Halsin is the subject of BG3 themed Magic The Gathering cards
